info.title: OpenLaw API
info.description: REST API for OpenLaw. Also the third-party integration surface (TECH-003).

get.summary: The signed-in user, with their live role and session

patch.summary: Update the signed-in user's preferences (theme #44, timezone SET-006)

get.summary: Whether first-run setup (initial Administrator) is still required

post.summary: First-run setup: create the initial Administrator

get.summary: What the login screen may offer (TECH-008): the auth mode, the magic-link toggle, whether outbound email works, and the SSO provider to start, if one is registered

post.summary: Invite a user (Administrator, Legal Team Member, or Contributor); re-sends the set-password email if they have not activated
Re-send a pending invite's set-password email (SET-005)

delete.summary: Revoke a pending invite (SET-005): the row is removed and the emailed set-password link stops working

post.summary: Register a bring-your-own OIDC identity provider (TECH-008); endpoint discovery runs from the issuer, and the response carries the callback URL to paste into the IdP console

get.summary: The registered OIDC identity providers (TECH-008), with their client IDs but never their secrets

patch.summary: Update the registered provider (TECH-008): omitted fields keep their stored values, endpoint discovery re-runs from the issuer, and a failed update leaves the provider untouched
Switch the auth mode (TECH-008): `oidc` closes password sign-in for everyone but Administrators (break-glass); switching never invalidates existing sessions

get.summary: The magic-link domain allowlist (DD-010); empty admits nobody

put.summary: Replace the magic-link domain allowlist (DD-010); the list is normalised to lower case and enforced on the next request — an empty list closes the portal to everyone

patch.summary: Open or close magic-link sign-in (DD-010's portal floor); takes effect on the next request, independent of the domain allowlist

post.summary: Request a portal magic link (DD-010); the response is identical whether or not the address is eligible

get.summary: First-run onboarding state (SET-004), plus whether email is configured

post.summary: Mark first-run onboarding finished (SET-004); idempotent, and never reversed — the wizard is first-run only

patch.summary: Update the organization's identity; applies immediately (SET-003) and appends one audit entry per changed field

get.summary: Every user with role, status, and last-active (SET-005); pending invites appear as rows with status `invited`

patch.summary: Change a user's role in place (SET-005); effective on the target's next request — the guard chain reads the role live

post.summary: Archive a user (SET-005): sign-in is blocked and every live session is revoked in the same operation
Restore an archived user (SET-003's recovery story): sign-in works again; the sessions archive revoked stay revoked
Revoke every live session of a user (SET-005's lost-laptop case); the account itself is untouched

get.summary: Where outbound email is configured (#37): environment, app, or not at all — and the effective from-address. Never the relay URL

put.summary: Save the app SMTP relay (#37): smtp:// or smtps:// URL with credentials inline, plus a from-address; both null clears. Takes effect on the next send. Refused while the environment pins SMTP — env always wins over app configuration

post.summary: Send a test email through the currently resolved mailer to the signed-in Administrator's own address (#37); fails loudly with a plain-language reason

get.summary: The contract-type taxonomy in display order (CTR-002); archived rows only with includeArchived=true

post.summary: Add a contract type: the slug is derived here, once, and is immutable after creation; the row appends to the display order

patch.summary: Rename a contract type's display name (DES-017 in-place rename); the slug never changes, and even `other` may rename

delete.summary: Hard-delete a contract type; `other` refuses (CTR-002), and once contracts exist (M8) an in-use type will refuse too

put.summary: Apply a full permutation of the live rows (SET-003 immediate apply); display orders renumber from 1, archived rows keep theirs

post.summary: Archive a contract type (SET-003 guarded): it leaves pickers and the default list; nothing is deleted; `other` refuses
Restore an archived contract type (SET-003's recovery story) to the end of the display order

get.summary: The contract-status taxonomy in display order (CTR-001), each row carrying its fixed stage; archived rows only with includeArchived=true

post.summary: Add a contract status: the stage is picked here, once, and is immutable after creation, like the derived slug; the row appends to the display order

patch.summary: Rename a contract status's display name (DES-017 in-place rename); the slug and the stage never change — a body carrying `stage` is refused, and even protected rows may rename

delete.summary: Hard-delete a contract status; the protected `draft`, `active`, and `expired` rows refuse (CTR-001), as does the last unarchived status of a stage

put.summary: Apply a full permutation of the live rows (SET-003 immediate apply); display orders renumber from 1, archived rows keep theirs

post.summary: Archive a contract status (SET-003): it leaves pickers and the default list; nothing is deleted. The last unarchived status of a stage refuses (CTR-001 floor), as do the protected `draft`, `active`, and `expired` rows — no reassignment, ever
Restore an archived contract status (SET-003's recovery story) to the end of the display order; its stage rides along unchanged
